findings.claim: The Decalogue establishes both duties to the Almighty (no other gods, no idols, no misuse of the divine name, observe Shabbat, honour parents) and duties to fellow human beings (no murder, adultery, theft, false testimony or coveting).
findings.truth: This is the Christian numbering, not the Jewish one. In the Jewish five-and-five division the first commandment is 'I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt', and 'no other gods' and 'no idols' are a single second commandment. The lesson drops the opening commandment altogether and splits the second in two.
findings.evidence: Exodus 20:2-17 in the Jewish (Talmudic) enumeration; spec 1.5 names Exodus 20 and requires understanding of the Decalogue in Jewish life

findings.claim: Talmud Yoma 83-84 … “If a person sees a child who has fallen into a well, he may break the Shabbat to save it.”
findings.truth: No such sentence exists in Yoma. The tractate gives concrete rescue cases: a child who falls into the sea is raised with a fisherman's net; a child who falls into a pit is dug out; a locked door is broken open to reach a frightened child - and the rescuer need not seek a court's permission. An invented quotation attributed to a named spec source.

findings.claim: The young person reads from the Torah scroll during a synagogue service for the first time - written of Bar Mitzvah and Bat Mitzvah alike
findings.truth: Orthodox synagogues do not allow women to read from the Torah, so an Orthodox Bat Mitzvah girl does not do this; her coming of age is usually marked by a study talk or a ceremony outside the main service. Reform and Liberal girls do read the Torah. The lesson's own practice question already says the Orthodox Bat Mitzvah is different, so the body text contradicts it.
findings.evidence: spec 2.5 (divergent understandings of each ritual in Orthodox and Reform Judaism); standard Orthodox practice on women reading Torah

findings.claim: Genesis 21:1-8 describes the birth and circumcision of Isaac as the first enactment of this covenant sign.
findings.truth: Abraham and Ishmael were circumcised first, in Genesis 17:23-27. Isaac was the first to be circumcised on the eighth day, which is the point Genesis 21 makes.

findings.truth: Abraham Joshua Heschel's phrase in The Sabbath is 'a palace in time'; separately he wrote 'The Sabbaths are our great cathedrals'. 'Cathedral in time' is a paraphrase, so the quotation marks make it a quotation he did not write. Rewritten without quotation marks.

findings.claim: Reform Jews are more likely to apply Pikuach Nefesh to mental health as well as physical health
findings.truth: Two readings. (a) As written it implies Orthodox halakha does not treat danger to mental health as pikuach nefesh, which is not so - Orthodox authorities do apply it to serious mental danger, case by case through a rabbi. (b) The looser claim that Reform reaches for the principle more readily in non-life-threatening hardship is defensible. Recommendation: keep the divergence but add that Orthodox authorities also accept serious mental danger, decided case by case.
findings.evidence: spec 1.6 requires divergent understandings of how Pikuach Nefesh is applied; standard Orthodox responsa practice

findings.claim: Distractor reads 'Torah, Prophets and Pirkei Avot' while the lesson body uses the spec's spelling 'Perkei Avot'
findings.truth: Inconsistent transliteration of the same tractate within one lesson. Both spellings are in use; the spec writes 'Perkei Avot'. Not mark-affecting.

findings.claim: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement) follows ten days later
findings.truth: Rosh Hashanah is 1-2 Tishrei and Yom Kippur is 10 Tishrei, so it falls on the tenth day rather than ten days afterwards. This is standard textbook shorthand and no exam mark turns on it, so it is left alone.

summary: No lesson misstates the paper's timing, marks or structure, and all sixteen spec-named sources are cited against the right content points; the twenty knowledge-check answer keys and all four match sets recompute correct. The damage is concentrated in two places: every 12-mark question across all four lessons uses the command word 'Discuss', which Edexcel does not use (the (d) part is Evaluate), and each lesson carries an invented '3 marks - Describe' question form that does not exist on this paper. Two hard content errors: the Ten Commandments are split in the Christian numbering rather than the Jewish five-and-five division that opens with 'I am the Lord your God' (L2), and a sentence that Yoma never contains is quoted as Talmud Yoma 83-84 (L2). Four scripture quotations blend NIV and JPS wordings and are pulled back to NIV.
